title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Finance and Bursary Administrator
company: Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited - Agency - Permanent
description:
Your new company

An exciting opportunity has arisen to join a highly regarded education and training organisation supporting the development of future professionals across the South West.

This organisation is known for its collaborative culture, commitment to personal development and supportive working environment, offering the opportunity to become part of a team that genuinely invests in its people.

Your new role

As a Finance & Bursary Administrator, you will play a key role in supporting both the financial and operational administration of a busy training programme.
You will be responsible for:
- Raising invoices and supporting day-to-day finance administration.
- Maintaining accurate financial records, spreadsheets and databases.
- Supporting funding and bursary administration processes.
- Assisting with payment schedules and reconciliations.
- Supporting trainee onboarding and record management.
- Administering trainee databases and ensuring information is maintained accurately.
- Responding to enquiries via telephone and email.
- Liaising with trainees, partner organisations and internal stakeholders.
- Supporting compliance, audit and reporting activities.
- Working closely with the Management Accountant and wider team.

This is a varied position combining finance administration, stakeholder engagement and programme support within a friendly and supportive environment.
What you'll need to succeedTo be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous finance administration, accounts administration or office administration experience.
- Strong customer service and stakeholder management skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Confidence maintaining accurate records and databases.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- The ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.
- A positive, resilient and proactive approach.

Experience within finance, accounts payable, purchase ledger, business support, education administration or customer-focused administration would be highly advantageous, although full training will be provided on the specialist elements of the role.
What you'll get in return
- £16.75 per hour PAYE Premium or £18.93 per hour Umbrella.
- 37 hours per week.
- 33 days annual leave.
- Free onsite parking.
- Onsite café and excellent facilities.
- Friendly and supportive team environment.
- Ongoing mentoring and development.
- Exposure to a broad range of finance and administrative responsibilities.
- Initial contract expected until Christmas with the potential for extension and longer-term opportunities.

title: Receptionist
description: Are you warm, organised and passionate about delivering exceptional first impressions? As our Receptionist, you will play an essential role in creating a professional, friendly and supportive experience for everyone who visits the hospital. You'll ensure all visitors are greeted politely, directed appropriately, and that the relevant staff are informed of their arrival promptly and efficiently. Alongside this, you'll provide administration support to managers, colleagues and service usershelping to keep our hospital running smoothly while ensuring compliance with organisational policies, procedures and best practice. Shift pattern hours - weekdays: 7:00am 3:00pm or 12:00midday 8:00pm and 1 in 3 weekends: 9:00am 5:00pm. The Receptionist role at Elysium Healthcare is integral to providing a professional and supportive experience for hospital visitors. As the initial point of contact, you will greet visitors, direct them appropriately, and inform relevant staff promptly. Administration support to managers, colleagues, and service users is required to ensure smooth hospital operations, adherence to policies, and best practices. The shift pattern includes weekdays from 7:00am-3:00pm or 12:00midday-8:00pm and every third weekend from 9:00am-5:00pm. Responsibilities include answering inbound calls, ensuring visitor sign-ins for health and safety, and managing key allocation. The role demands professional conduct, relationship building, stress management, confidentiality, accuracy, and software proficiency. title: Administrator
description: At Sentinel Healthcare, delivering excellent patient care is at the heart of everything we do. We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic Administrator to join our friendly and supportive team, providing high-quality administrative and reception support across our clinical services. This varied and rewarding role involves supporting patients, clinicians and colleagues to ensure services run smoothly and efficiently. You will often be the first point of contact for patients, so a professional, compassionate and customer-focused approach is essential. The successful candidate will be organised, adaptable and able to manage multiple tasks in a busy environment. Excellent communication, attention to detail and strong IT skills are essential, along with the ability to work accurately and build positive relationships with patients, colleagues and partner organisations. We are looking for a supportive team player who is willing to work flexibly and contribute to a positive working environment. Previous experience in healthcare administration, particularly within primary or secondary care, would be advantageous. By joining Sentinel Healthcare, you will become part of a close-knit team that genuinely cares about making a difference to patients and the communities we serve. If you are looking for a rewarding role where your contribution is valued and every day brings something different, we would love to hear from you. Process electronic inbound referrals from GP's and other healthcare organisations using patient record systems. Booking and managing of patient appointments. Deal with routine patient enquiries. Ensure that electronic tasks are completed in a timely manner. Assist in monitoring generic email accounts. Send text reminder messages/emails to patients. Supporting Senior Administrative colleagues. Attending administrative and clinical meetings as required, which may occasionally be outside of core working hours. General office duties, such as post, scanning etc. Use the e-Referrals system (eRS) and the Electronic Patient Record systems (EMIS & SystmOne) to access inbound referrals and associated clinical documents booked in the Sentinel Healthcare clinical services. Liaise with local Referral Management Centres, GP surgeries and other external organisations as necessary. Using own judgement bring any GP referrals which may be inappropriate to the Clinician(s) attention. Ensure that inbound referrals are appropriately actioned i.e. accepted or rejected. Assist in co-ordinating the utilisation of booking slots across service areas, ensuring that capacity is fully utilised. Any under-utilisation to be reported promptly to the Operations Manager, so that appropriate action can be taken in advance. Re-book and cancel appointments as necessary in the patient record system and ERS. Any cancellations are to be undertaken following the set criteria for the service. Attention should be given to waiting time. Patients must be rebooked within specified time scales. Any problems meeting these criteria, including late cancellations, should be highlighted immediately to the Administration Manager. Ensure that relevant reminders (either by SMS, email or letter, where appropriate) have been sent to patients informing them of appointments. Ensure investigation requests are processed appropriately and results shown to the referring clinician. Assist in completing clinical coding and outcomes. Assist in using the patient record system to ensure that clinical reports and templates are re-produced and sent to GPs (and patients if required) following consultations. Open and prioritise correspondence, ensuring urgent correspondence receives prompt attention. Scan reports and other correspondence into the patient record system in a timely manner. Work closely with service area colleagues/clinicians to ensure good communication and that tasks are appropriately allocated and completed in a timely manner. Adherence to Sentinel Referral to Treatment Rulebook, Referral to Treatment Access Policy and to National Referral to Treat (RTT) waiting times rules and assist in making sure those targets are met. Assist in ensuring that Inter-Provider Transfer Forms (IPT) are completed and sent, as soon as the clinician requests onward referral to Secondary Care, in line with Waiting List Policy (48 working hours). Use other local hospital systems as necessary e.g, EPIC. Ensure that generic service nhs.net email accounts are monitored daily and appropriate action taken in a timely manner. Liaise with GP(s) or their team(s) when removing patients from the waiting lists as per protocols Have a sympathetic and caring manner when dealing with patients, ensuring all queries are handled timely, efficiently and effectively. Deal with telephone queries from both internal and external agencies in a professional manner in accordance with GDPR and statutory policies and procedures. To deal with all enquiries and complaints promptly and sympathetically and inform Senior Management of any problems immediately. Record accurate patient messages and complete information using the patient record system in a timely manner. Request hospital patient case notes (where requested by clinicians) ensuring that relevant clinical documentation (e.g. referral letter, x-rays, other diagnostic results and other supporting information) is available to the clinical teams in the patient record system. Maintain patient case notes and other documentation in good order and arrange return appropriately and in a timely manner. Assist in arranging and attending MDT meetings (where necessary) and ensure that patient notes, investigations and radiology images are available. Work flexibly and collaboratively with colleagues and help to develop a positive, supportive culture. Be prepared to work at various locations to provide appropriate administrative support to clinical teams as required. Attend and contribute positively and creatively to Administration Meetings. Demonstrate a positive, can-do attitude in the workplace. Ensure that resources are used efficiently and help to identify cost savings. Attend and represent Sentinel at external meetings as required Maintain an efficient electronic filing system. Responsible for covering colleagues during periods of annual leave and sickness. Undertake work as directed by the Administration Manager. Adhere to Patient Confidentiality, Information Governance and GDPR policies at all times.

title: Reception/Administrator
description: We are looking for someone with excellent communication and interpersonal skills, who can engage with patients in a professional, compassionate and empathetic manner. The ideal candidate will be resilient, adaptable, and able to manage competing demands while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. A positive, team-focused attitude and a genuine commitment to patient care are key to succeeding in this role. Whilst previous administrative or reception experience is desirable, we are also keen to hear from applicants with limited or no direct experience, as this minimum 12-month maternity cover position provides an excellent opportunity to develop administrative, communication and patient-facing skills within a busy GP practice. We are seeking a confident, proactive, and highly organised Administrator to join our busy GP practice team. This is a fast-paced and dynamic front-line role, where no two days are the same, and the ability to stay calm under pressure is essential. As the first point of contact for our patients, you will pay a vital role in creating a welcoming, respectful and efficient environment. The working pattern for this fixed term 12-month maternity cover (full time) is as follows:- Monday 8.15am - 5.15pm (with 1 hour lunch break) Tuesday 8.15am - 5.15pm (with 1 hour lunch break) Wednesday 8.15am - 12.15pm Thursday 8.15am - 6.30pm (with 1 1/4 hours lunch break) Friday 8.15am - 5.15pm (with 1 hour lunch break) Starting pay of £12.71 per hour. On successful completion of probationary period this will increase to £12.81 per hour. Closing date Friday 16th October. Successful applicants will be contacted by the end of the working day on 19th October at the latest. Interviews are planned for Wednesday 21st and Thursday 22nd October. The interview process will include group interviews on the Wednesday and formal interviews on the Thursday for those short listed following the group stage. Job Title: Healthcare Administrator to the Nursing Team REPORTS TO: Healthcare Administration Manager/Deputy HOURS: 37 hours per week Job Summary The purpose of the role is to: Offer general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way by telephone and on the helpdesk Undertake a variety of administrative duties to assist in the smooth running of the Practice including the provision of clerical support to clinical staff and other members of the Practice team Facilitate effective communication between patients, members the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies Duties and Responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the Practice administration team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the Healthcare Admin Manager, Deputy, Practice Manager, dependent on current and evolving Practice workload and staffing levels: Maintaining security in accordance with Practice protocols Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail Taking messages and passing on information Filing and retrieving paperwork Computer data entry/data allocation and collation; processing and recording information in accordance with Practice procedures Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team member and associated healthcare agencies and providers Clearing and re-stock consulting rooms as required Assist in preparation & setting up of the working environment & nursing clinical rooms for appropriate procedures & maintaining the organisation of them Set up clinic templates on to the IT system Co-ordinating the ordering & maintaining supplies used within the nursing team Providing clerical assistance to Practice staff as required from time to time, including word/data processing, filing, photocopying and scanning Ordering, re-ordering and monitoring of stationery and other supplies Dealing with clinical waste in line with practice health and safety policy Keeping the reception areas, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter Attending departmental meetings Other duties as required by the line manager Underpinning Policies Confidentiality: Adhere to the General Data Protection Regulations (GDPR) May 2018. In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk and contribute to the practice risk register as needed Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognize peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate This job description may be subject to change from time to time to reflect the changing needs of the Practice, but it is a correct reflection of the type of duties that need to be undertaken. Litchdon Mission Statement Providing quality healthcare by valuing both patients and staff in a supportive and sustainable environment. Litchdon Values Compassionate Care We treat staff, patients, carers, and relatives with kindness, respect, and dignity, fostering a culture of mutual empathy. Holistic wellbeing We prioritise the physical, mental, and emotional wellbeing of our staff which then enables them to deliver person centred care. Positive reliable teams We cultivate professional, approachable, and cohesive teams built on loyalty, trust, and mutual respect, enabling them to deliver safe and effective care to patients. Family focussed We support the work-life balance of our staff and recognise the importance of family for patients and colleagues alike. Innovation and Growth We embrace change, prioritise sustainability, and nurture professional development across the workforce to improve processes and patient care. Environmental Responsibility We are mindful and committed to be as eco-friendly as possible by ensuring we consider the impact of our practice on both the community and the planet. title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: Receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist/administrator are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record We are offering this role on a temp to perm basis and would consider a job share.
